prompt:
I need the front end for Nightfeed Notes. A baby-care logging app that new parents share between them to record feeds, sleep and nappies, and then look back at the patterns to make decisions about routines.

Who's using it: Tomasz and Claire Nowak, first-time parents in Manchester. It's Claire using it right now: on maternity leave, sleep-deprived, comfortable with spreadsheets from her job in logistics, but with no patience left for anything fiddly.

What they're doing right now: Their daughter Zosia is 11 weeks old. The health visitor suggested they might be able to drop the 3am feed if Zosia is taking enough in the evening. Claire wants to find out from their own records whether bigger last-evening feeds actually lead to a longer first sleep stretch. She also wants to know if the 3am wake-up has been getting later over the past three weeks, and whether nights when Tomasz did the bedtime bottle look different from nights she breastfed. She wants to single out the bad nights and see what the evening before looked like, then show Tomasz what she finds before they try a new routine on Monday.

What's in the system at this point: 11 weeks of shared records (6 Sep–21 Nov 2026). 712 feeds, each with start time, duration or millilitres (bottle: expressed milk or formula; breast: side and minutes), and who logged it. 498 sleep stretches with start and end times. 603 nappy entries (wet/dirty). 5 weigh-ins from the health visitor (3.4 kg at birth to 5.6 kg at week 10). Notes on 9 nights (e.g., 'jabs today', 'growth spurt?'). Evening bottle sizes range 60–150 ml. The first night stretch ranges from 2h10m to 5h45m. Tomasz logged 41% of evening feeds.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
